sourcedFrom: SilencerCo Osprey Micro Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. (2015)
cleanIntro:
The Osprey Micro is built to be taken apart. One allen key takes the sex bolt out of the front cap, the baffles slide off a central rod, and the rod unscrews from the back cap: that is the whole can, and SilencerCo calls it user-serviceable. Their interval is 1,000 rounds, sooner with dirty ammunition.

The book allows more than most: solvents, light abrasive media, chemical dips, even abrasive pads and wire brushes, as long as you test a hidden spot first. The things it insists on are on the way back together: clean baffle edges, the rod through the right hole, cones toward the back cap, no step in the stack, and every part dry.

steps.title: Action open, firearm empty, before the can is touched
steps.action: Open the host's action, make sure it is unloaded, and look into the chamber. This comes before maintenance, before removal and before installation.
steps.prose: A suppressed gun is quieter, not safer. The book is plain that the same safe-handling rules apply, and that if you are unsure how to unload your particular host, its own manual is where to look.
steps.quote: Before performing maintenance, removing, or installing the suppressor, open the action, ensure firearm is unloaded, and be sure the chamber is empty.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Osprey Micro Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — Warnings, PDF p.9

steps.title: ⛔ It may be hot — gloves or the Nomex sleeve
steps.action: Treat the can as hot until you have proved it is not. Use gloves or the Nomex sleeve that came with it to take it off.
steps.prose: A .22 can keeps its heat well after the barrel feels cool, and the hand that unscrews it is wrapped right around it.
steps.quote: When removing the Osprey Micro, use extreme caution as it may be hot to the touch after firing. Use gloves, or the provided Nomex suppressor sleeve, to avoid burns or other injuries.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Osprey Micro Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — Warnings, PDF p.9

steps.title: ⛔ Off the host completely before anything comes apart
steps.action: Unscrew the Osprey Micro from the Rapid Attach Adapter and take it right off the gun. Nothing on the can is opened while it is still mounted.
steps.prose: Opening the can on the gun means working around the muzzle with tools, and the book forbids it outright.
steps.quote: Always completely remove the Osprey Micro from the host firearm before assembly and/or disassembly is attempted.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Osprey Micro Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — Warnings, PDF p.9

steps.title: If the adapter came off with the can, take it out
steps.action: Sometimes the Rapid Attach Adapter stays in the can instead of on the barrel. Seat the raised part of the provided tool in the notches at the rear of the adapter and turn counterclockwise.
steps.prose: If the adapter stayed on the barrel, skip this. If you leave it on the barrel between cleanings, its shim timing stays set and the can comes back to the same orientation.
steps.quote: Turn counterclockwise to loosen the adapter and remove from the silencer.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Osprey Micro Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — ADAPTER REMOVAL, PDF p.15

steps.title: Sex bolt out of the front cap
steps.action: With the supplied allen key, unscrew the sex bolt from the front cap. Hold the can muzzle-up or over a tray.
steps.prose: As soon as the bolt is out, the stack loosens and the baffles start to slide off the rod on their own. Do not let them fall onto a hard floor.
steps.aside: Note: The baffles will begin to fit together loosely at this point and will start to slide off of the internal rod.
steps.quote: remove the sex bolt (2D) from the front cap of the Osprey Micro.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Osprey Micro Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — CHANGING LENGTHS, PDF p.16

steps.title: Baffles off the rod, then the rod out of the back cap
steps.action: Slide the front cap and each baffle off the internal rod, then unscrew the rod from the back cap.
steps.prose: This is the book's own disassembly. It is printed under CHANGING LENGTHS, and the maintenance page tells you to disassemble the can 'as listed above'. Keep the baffles in order and note which way the cones face, because they go back cone-first toward the back cap.
steps.quote: Once all baffles are removed, unscrew the 4.6" configuration internal rod (2E) from the back cap.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Osprey Micro Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — CHANGING LENGTHS, PDF p.17

steps.title: Every 1,000 rounds, sooner with dirty ammunition
steps.action: Plan the full strip-and-clean around 1,000 rounds, and shorten that if your ammunition is dirty.
steps.prose: .22 ammunition varies a lot in how much lead and wax it leaves behind, so the book gives a starting number and says it may need to be more often.
steps.quote: SilencerCo recommends cleaning the Osprey Micro after 1,000 rounds, although greater frequency might be needed depending on the type of ammunition used.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Osprey Micro Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — MAINTENANCE, PDF p.19

steps.title: Baffles, rod and caps: solvent, light abrasive or a dip
steps.action: Clean the baffles, the rod and both caps with solvent, light abrasive media or a chemical dip, until the carbon and lead are off.
steps.prose: The book allows more methods than most suppressor makers do.
steps.quote: The Osprey Micro internal components can be cleaned using solvents, light abrasive media, or certain chemical dips.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Osprey Micro Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — MAINTENANCE, PDF p.19

steps.title: Pads and wire brushes are allowed, but test a hidden spot first
steps.action: Before you scrub a whole baffle with an abrasive pad or wire brush, try it on a spot nobody sees and check that it does not scratch the finish.
steps.prose: The test spot is the condition the book puts on using them.
steps.quote: The use of abrasive pads or wire brushes is acceptable, but a small test should be done on an inconspicuous area to ensure no scratching or damage will occur to the metal finish.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Osprey Micro Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — MAINTENANCE, PDF p.19

steps.title: Discolored outside: wipe with gun oil
steps.action: If the outer tube's finish has gone discolored, wipe it down with a good gun oil.
steps.prose: According to the book, this should bring the finish back to how it left the factory.
steps.quote: If the finish of the outer tube becomes discolored, wipe the suppressor with any high quality gun oil; this should restore the finish to the factory condition.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Osprey Micro Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — MAINTENANCE, PDF p.19

steps.title: ⛔ Dry everything before it goes back together
steps.action: Let every part dry completely after solvent or a dip, inside the baffle cones included, before you start reassembling.
steps.prose: The book gives this one instruction about finishing the clean, and it applies to every part.
steps.quote: Dry all components thoroughly before reassembling.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Osprey Micro Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — MAINTENANCE, PDF p.19

steps.title: Rod into the back cap, baffles on with clean edges
steps.action: Screw the internal rod for the length you want, 4.6" or 3.1", into the back cap. Before each baffle goes on, check that its edges are free of debris, and that the rod is not passing through the baffle's bore.
steps.prose: Grit on a baffle edge holds the stack apart, and a baffle threaded onto the rod through its bore is in the bullet's path.
steps.quote: ensuring that all baffle edges are clear of debris, ensuring that the threaded rod is NOT through the bore of the baffle.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Osprey Micro Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — CHANGING LENGTHS, PDF p.17

steps.title: ⛔ Cones toward the back cap, no step in the stack
steps.action: Seat every baffle with its cone end facing the back cap, nested tight to the one before, so the outside of the stack is flush with no step anywhere.
steps.prose: A step means a baffle is crooked, and a crooked baffle is how a bullet ends up hitting one.
steps.quote: The baffles must be seated together so that no misalignment or step is created.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Osprey Micro Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — CHANGING LENGTHS, PDF p.18

steps.title: Front cap on, sex bolt tight
steps.action: Seat the front cap over the end of the rod, thread the sex bolt onto the rod with the allen key, and tighten it until it is secure.
steps.prose: The book gives no torque figure, only that it must be secure.
steps.quote: onto the threads of the internal rod. Tighten until secure.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Osprey Micro Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — CHANGING LENGTHS, PDF p.18

steps.title: Back on the host, mark to the front sight
steps.action: Thread the Osprey Micro onto the Rapid Attach Adapter and check the alignment: the reference mark on top of the back cap should line up with the front sight.
steps.prose: If it does not line up, the book's ALIGNING section and the EasyAlign tool tell you which shims to put behind the adapter.
steps.quote: The reference mark on the top of the Osprey Micro back cap should align with the front sight post
steps.cite: SilencerCo Osprey Micro Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — SILENCER INSTALLATION, PDF p.14

steps.title: ⛔ No gap at the barrel shoulder — check before firing
steps.action: Look where the thread mount meets the barrel shoulder. It must be fully shouldered, with no visible gap. If there is a gap, do not fire.
steps.prose: The book says poor accuracy and damage to the can follow if it is not fully shouldered.
steps.quote: There should be no visible gap between the barrel shoulder and the face of the suppressor thread mount.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Osprey Micro Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — Warnings, PDF p.9

deepAbsentReason: The book publishes one disassembly: the CHANGING LENGTHS procedure (PDF pp.16-18: sex bolt out of the front cap, baffles off the internal rod, rod out of the back cap). Its MAINTENANCE page (PDF p.19) points back to that procedure for cleaning. Those parts are the whole can, and the book prints nothing beyond them, so there is no separate deeper procedure.

cleaning.name: INTERNAL COMPONENTS
tasks: Baffles, internal rod, front cap and back cap cleaned with solvent, light abrasive media or a chemical dip
Abrasive pads and wire brushes allowed: test a hidden spot first
Every baffle edge clear of debris before it goes back on the rod
⛔ Every component dried thoroughly before reassembly

cleaning.name: OUTER TUBE
tasks: Discolored finish wiped with a high-quality gun oil

reassembly: Internal rod for the length you want (4.6" or 3.1") screwed into the back cap.
Baffles slid onto the rod, edges clean, the rod never through a baffle's bore, cone ends facing the back cap.
Stack seated tight, with no misalignment or step anywhere along it.
Front cap seated over the rod, sex bolt threaded on with the allen key and tightened until secure.
Rapid Attach Adapter on the barrel (with its shims), the can threaded onto it, and the back-cap reference mark lined up with the front sight.
⛔ Fully shouldered, with no visible gap at the barrel shoulder, before the first shot.
fncheck: SilencerCo's book prints no function check for the can. Before firing it has you check three things: the reference mark on the back cap lines up with the host's front sight, the thread mount sits fully on the barrel shoulder with no visible gap, and nothing is blocking the can.
